openings.claim: Unreliable reader-to-location addresses drive retrieval delay: household surnames and stale exceptions trigger repeat searches. O4 remains intact: newly arrived cart books can have fresh, reliable addresses despite being unshelved.
openings.delta: Treat divider narrowing and exception accuracy as an address-reliability problem; shelving alone is not the proposed remedy.
openings.prediction: At comparable book size and candidate count, incorrect first addresses cause substantially longer searches; reliable shelf and cart addresses perform similarly.
openings.rival_prediction: Search-set density dominates: at comparable address reliability, crowded shelf regions remain slower than sparse carts; address errors explain little residual delay.
openings.defeat: Reliable shelf addresses remain slow while unreliable cart addresses remain fast after matching book size and candidate count.
openings.probe: One shared bounded observational probe: the existing clerk uses the timing sheet to record anonymous pickup duration, search duration, initial-address accuracy, candidate count and book size during ordinary handoffs. Compare naturally occurring episodes matched on size/count and, separately, on address accuracy. Keep all identifying material behind the desk, retain normal identity checks, use existing furniture, and cap total daily preparation including setup at ten minutes.
assumptions: Brief recording is feasible without materially delaying pickups.
This evaluates the bounded probe; an intervention achieving 95% within two minutes remains unproven.

openings.claim: Candidate-set density and handling difficulty dominate retrieval delay. O4 may reflect small, accessible arrival batches; shelf crowding can prolong both first and second searches. O2/O3 remain real address errors, potentially secondary contributors.
openings.delta: Challenge equal storage/search conditions rather than treating every extra search as evidence of address failure.
openings.prediction: Within address-accuracy and size matches, larger candidate sets predict longer searches; cart speed disappears when density is comparable.
openings.rival_prediction: Address unreliability dominates: size/count-matched wrong-address episodes remain slower, while density adds little once addresses are reliable.
openings.defeat: Wrong-address episodes remain substantially slower at matched size/count, with no meaningful density gradient among reliable addresses.
openings.probe: Use the same observational probe and comparison specified in A1; the disputed observation is whether address accuracy or candidate density retains the stronger association after matching.
assumptions: Cart volume and book-size explanations are unverified.
Probe fit does not establish faster correct handoffs for readers or reduced clerk burden.
